variant: K9 Vajra-T (Indian variant of Samsung Techwin K9 Thunder)

header.one_liner: 155mm/52-cal tracked self-propelled howitzer; 100 delivered (₹4,500 cr 2017), 100 more ordered (₹7,629 cr Dec 2024); 82%+ indigenous content by April 2026; deployed in Eastern Ladakh high-altitude.

what_it_is.prose: The K9 Vajra-T is a 155mm/52-calibre tracked self-propelled howitzer produced by Larsen & Toubro (L&T) under a co-development and Transfer of Technology agreement with Hanwha Aerospace of South Korea (originally Samsung Techwin). The K9 Vajra-T is the Indian variant of the K9 Thunder, customized for Indian conditions including desert, high-altitude, and tropical operations. The howitzer has a range of 30 km (standard), 40 km (base-bleed), or 50 km (V-LAP), with a maximum rate of fire of 6-8 rounds per minute and Multiple Rounds Simultaneous Impact (MRSI) capability of 3 rounds in 15 seconds. The platform is powered by an MTU MT881 Ka-500 diesel engine (Germany / South Korea) producing 1,000 hp, with a road speed of 67 km/h. The first batch of 100 K9 Vajra-T was delivered ahead of schedule under a ₹4,500 crore 2017 contract; a repeat order for 100 more was signed on 23 December 2024 for ₹7,629 crore (PIB confirmation 20 December 2024). As of April 2026, the K9 Vajra-T programme has achieved 82%+ indigenous content at the work-package level — a significant milestone for the Make in India programme. Manufacturing is at the L&T Armoured Systems Complex in Hazira, Gujarat — the first private defence ASC in India. The K9 Vajra-T has been deployed operationally in Eastern Ladakh following the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, demonstrating its high-altitude capability. The K9 programme represents India's largest artillery induction since the Bofors FH-77B controversy of the 1980s.

The first batch of 100 was delivered ahead of schedule. As of April 2026, the programme achieved 82%+ indigenous content at the work-package level. The K9 Vajra-T has been deployed operationally in Eastern Ladakh following the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.

faq.question: What is the K9 Vajra-T and why is it significant?
faq.answer: The K9 Vajra-T is a 155mm/52-calibre tracked self-propelled howitzer produced by L&T under a co-development and Transfer of Technology agreement with Hanwha Aerospace of South Korea. It is the Indian variant of the K9 Thunder. The K9 Vajra-T is significant because it represents India's largest artillery induction since the Bofors FH-77B controversy of the 1980s, with 200 units ordered (₹4,500 cr 2017 + ₹7,629 cr December 2024 = ₹12,129 crore aggregate). The programme achieved 82%+ indigenous content by April 2026 — a major Make in India milestone.

faq.question: Where is the K9 Vajra-T manufactured?
faq.answer: The K9 Vajra-T is manufactured at the L&T Armoured Systems Complex (ASC) in Hazira, Gujarat — the first private defence ASC in India. The facility was inaugurated in 2018 specifically for the K9 Vajra-T programme. Hanwha Aerospace of South Korea supplies the engine and certain components under a $253 million second contract (for the 100 repeat-order units); L&T manufactures the rest in India with progressive indigenisation reaching 82% by April 2026.

faq.question: Has the K9 Vajra-T been deployed operationally?
faq.answer: Yes. The K9 Vajra-T has been deployed to Eastern Ladakh following the 2020 Galvan Valley clash with China, demonstrating its high-altitude operational capability. The howitzer's tracked platform and 1,000 hp engine allow it to operate in mountainous terrain where towed howitzers cannot easily reach. The Indian Army has integrated the K9 Vajra-T into its artillery regiments alongside the indigenous ATAGS (Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System) and the M777 ultra-light howitzer (BAE Systems, USA).
